9	/-!
10	# Faithfully flat descent of modules
11	
12	Let `A → B` be a map of commutative rings and let `M` be a `B`-module.  This file defines
13	descent data on `M` relative to `A → B`, constructs the descended `A`-module `M₀` as an
14	equalizer submodule of `M`, and proves the two fundamental theorems of flat descent for
15	modules:
16	
17	* **effectivity**: if `B` is flat over `A`, the canonical comparison map
18	  `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism;
19	* **uniqueness**: if `B` is faithfully flat over `A`, then any `A`-module `N` equipped with
20	  a `B`-module isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ M` matching the descent datum is canonically
21	  isomorphic to `M₀`.  The engine is the degree `≤ 1` exactness of the Amitsur complex
22	  `0 → N → B ⊗[A] N ⇉ B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] N`.
23	
24	## Design notes
25	
26	* **Comodule form of a descent datum.**  Classically a descent datum on `M` is a
27	  `B ⊗[A] B`-module isomorphism `φ : M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M` satisfying a cocycle condition
28	  over the triple tensor product.  We use the equivalent *comodule* (Sweedler-coring)
29	  presentation: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M` (with `B` acting on the left
30	  tensor factor of the target) such that
31	  - (`counit`) the action map `B ⊗[A] M → M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, retracts `δ`, and
32	  - (`coassoc`) the two natural liftings of `δ` to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on the image
33	    of `δ`.
34	
35	  The dictionary: given `φ`, set `δ m := φ (m ⊗ₜ 1)`; then `B ⊗ B`-linearity of `φ` makes
36	  `δ` `B`-linear and recovers `φ` via `φ (m ⊗ₜ b) = (1 ⊗ b) • δ m`, the cocycle condition
37	  becomes `coassoc`, and the standard normalization becomes `counit`.  Conversely the `φ`
38	  associated to a coaction is automatically invertible.  This presentation avoids putting
39	  (several!) `B ⊗[A] B`-module structures on `B ⊗[A] M` and `M ⊗[A] B`, which do not exist
40	  as mathlib instances.  For a unit `u : (B ⊗[A] B)ˣ` whose associated `φ` is
41	  `u • ·` on `M = B`, the coaction is `δ x = u.val * (x ⊗ₜ 1)`.
42	
43	* **The descended module** is the equalizer `M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`, an `A`-submodule
44	  of `M`, realized as the kernel of the `A`-linear map `δ - (1 ⊗ₜ ·)`.
45	
46	* **Effectivity requires only flatness.**  The comparison `B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` is an isomorphism
47	  whenever `B` is flat over `A`: the counit and coassociativity laws make the augmented
48	  complex `M₀ → M ⇉ B ⊗[A] M` contractible after applying `B ⊗[A] -` (the contraction being
49	  the action maps), and flatness identifies `B ⊗[A] M₀` with the corresponding kernel.
50	  Faithful flatness enters only for uniqueness (the Amitsur exactness `N ≅ (B ⊗[A] N)₀`).
51	
52	* Everything is pinned to a single universe `u`; multi-universe binders interact badly with
53	  the tensor-product instance search in downstream files.
54	
55	## Main declarations
56	
57	* `Module.actionMap A B M : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`: the action map `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
58	* `Module.DescentDatum A B M`: descent data on the `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`,
59	  in comodule form.
60	* `Module.DescentDatum.baseChange A B N`: the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N`.
61	* `Module.DescentDatum.descended`: the descended `A`-submodule `M₀`.
62	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison`: the canonical map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.
63	* `Module.DescentDatum.comparison_bijective`: **effectivity** — `comparison` is bijective
64	  when `B` is a flat `A`-module.
65	* `Module.DescentDatum.descentEquiv : B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ₗ[B] M`: the comparison isomorphism.
66	* `Module.DescentDatum.exact_mk_coactionSub`: degree `≤ 1` **Amitsur exactness** for a
67	  faithfully flat `A → B`.
68	* `Module.DescentDatum.unitEquiv : N ≃ₗ[A] (baseChange A B N).descended`: the unit of
69	  descent is an isomorphism (faithfully flat case).
70	* `Module.DescentDatum.equivDescended`: **uniqueness** — an `A`-module `N` with a
71	  datum-compatible isomorphism `B ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[B] M` is canonically `A`-isomorphic to `M₀`.
72	  Two descents of the same datum are therefore canonically isomorphic.
73	-/

75	universe u
76	
77	open TensorProduct
78	
79	namespace Module
80	
81	variable (A B : Type u) [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B]
82	variable (M : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module B M] [IsScalarTower A B M]
83	
84	/-- The `B`-linear action map `B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`, of a `B`-module `M`. -/
85	noncomputable def actionMap : B ⊗[A] M →ₗ[B] M :=
86	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B (LinearMap.id (R := A) (M := M))
87	
88	@[simp] theorem actionMap_tmul (b : B) (m : M) : actionMap A B M (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • m := rfl
89	
90	theorem actionMap_one_tmul (m : M) : actionMap A B M (1 ⊗ₜ m) = m := by simp
91	
92	variable {A B M}
93	
94	section actionMap
95	
96	variable {X Y : Type u} [AddCommGroup X] [Module A X]
97	
98	/-- Naturality of the action map in `B`-linear maps. -/
99	theorem actionMap_baseChange [Module B X] [IsScalarTower A B X]
100	    [AddCommGroup Y] [Module A Y] [Module B Y] [IsScalarTower A B Y]
101	    (g : X →ₗ[B] Y) (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
102	    actionMap A B Y ((g.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x) = g (actionMap A B X x) := by
103	  induction x with
104	  | zero => simp
105	  | tmul b m => simp
106	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
107	
108	/-- The action map of `B ⊗[A] X` retracts the base change of `x ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ x`. -/
109	theorem actionMap_baseChange_mk (x : B ⊗[A] X) :
110	    actionMap A B (B ⊗[A] X) ((TensorProduct.mk A B X 1).baseChange B x) = x := by
111	  induction x with
112	  | zero => simp
113	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
114	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
115	
116	end actionMap
117	
118	variable (A B M) in
119	/-- A descent datum on a `B`-module `M` relative to `A → B`, in comodule (Sweedler-coring)
120	form: a `B`-linear coaction `δ : M → B ⊗[A] M` (`B` acting through the left tensor factor
121	of the target) that is counital and coassociative.  This is equivalent to the classical
122	formulation via a `B ⊗[A] B`-linear cocycle isomorphism `M ⊗[A] B ≃ B ⊗[A] M`; see the
123	module docstring for the dictionary. -/
124	structure DescentDatum where
125	  /-- The coaction of the descent datum. -/
126	  coaction : M →ₗ[B] B ⊗[A] M
127	  /-- The action map retracts the coaction. -/
128	  counit (m : M) : actionMap A B M (coaction m) = m
129	  /-- Coassociativity: the two liftings of the coaction to `B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] M` agree on
130	  coaction values.  In the classical dictionary this is the cocycle condition. -/
131	  coassoc (m : M) :
132	    (coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B (coaction m) =
133	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B (coaction m)
134	
135	namespace DescentDatum
136	
137	variable (A B) in
138	/-- The canonical descent datum on a base change `B ⊗[A] N`, with coaction
139	`b ⊗ₜ n ↦ b ⊗ₜ 1 ⊗ₜ n`. -/
140	@[simps coaction]
141	noncomputable def baseChange (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
142	    DescentDatum A B (B ⊗[A] N) where
143	  coaction := (TensorProduct.mk A B N 1).baseChange B
144	  counit x := by
145	    induction x with
146	    | zero => simp
147	    | tmul b n => simp [TensorProduct.smul_tmul']
148	    | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
149	  coassoc x := by
150	    induction x with
151	    | zero => simp
152	    | tmul b n => simp
153	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
154	
155	variable (D : DescentDatum A B M)
156	
157	/-- The `A`-linear difference between the coaction and the canonical map `m ↦ 1 ⊗ₜ m`;
158	its kernel is the descended module. -/
159	def coactionSub : M →ₗ[A] B ⊗[A] M :=
160	  D.coaction.restrictScalars A - TensorProduct.mk A B M 1
161	
162	@[simp] theorem coactionSub_apply (m : M) : D.coactionSub m = D.coaction m - 1 ⊗ₜ m := rfl
163	
164	/-- The descended `A`-module of a descent datum: the equalizer
165	`M₀ = {m : M | δ m = 1 ⊗ₜ m}`. -/
166	def descended : Submodule A M := LinearMap.ker D.coactionSub
167	
168	theorem mem_descended {m : M} : m ∈ D.descended ↔ D.coaction m = 1 ⊗ₜ m := by
169	  rw [descended, LinearMap.mem_ker, coactionSub_apply, sub_eq_zero]
170	
171	/-- The canonical comparison map `B ⊗[A] M₀ →ₗ[B] M`, `b ⊗ₜ m ↦ b • m`.  Flat descent
172	(`comparison_bijective`) asserts this is an isomorphism when `B` is flat over `A`. -/
173	noncomputable def comparison : B ⊗[A] D.descended →ₗ[B] M :=
174	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange B D.descended.subtype
175	
176	@[simp] theorem comparison_tmul (b : B) (m : D.descended) :
177	    D.comparison (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • (m : M) := rfl
178	
179	theorem comparison_eq_actionMap (x : B ⊗[A] D.descended) :
180	    D.comparison x = actionMap A B M (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B x) := by
181	  induction x with
182	  | zero => simp
183	  | tmul b m => simp
184	  | add x y hx hy => simp [hx, hy]
185	
186	private theorem coactionSub_lTensor_apply (x : B ⊗[A] M) :
187	    D.coactionSub.lTensor B x =
188	      (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x -
189	        (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x := by
190	  induction x with
191	  | zero => simp
192	  | tmul b m => simp [TensorProduct.tmul_sub]
193	  | add x y hx hy =>
194	      simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
195	      abel
196	
197	/-- The coaction retracts onto the kernel of `coactionSub ⊗ B`: any `x : B ⊗[A] M` on which
198	the two liftings agree is a coaction value, namely of `actionMap x`.  This is the
199	contracting-homotopy computation at the heart of both effectivity and Amitsur exactness. -/
200	theorem coaction_actionMap {x : B ⊗[A] M}
201	    (hx : (D.coaction.restrictScalars A).baseChange B x =
202	      (TensorProduct.mk A B M 1).baseChange B x) :
203	    D.coaction (actionMap A B M x) = x :=
204	  (actionMap_baseChange D.coaction x).symm.trans <| by rw [hx, actionMap_baseChange_mk]
205	
206	/-- **Effectivity of flat descent for modules**: for `B` flat over `A`, the canonical map
207	`B ⊗[A] M₀ → M` out of the descended module is bijective. -/
208	theorem comparison_bijective [Module.Flat A B] : Function.Bijective D.comparison := by
209	  have hexact : Function.Exact (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) (D.coactionSub.lTensor B) :=
210	    Module.Flat.lTensor_exact B D.coactionSub.exact_subtype_ker_map
211	  have hinj : Function.Injective (D.descended.subtype.lTensor B) :=
212	    Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ D.descended.injective_subtype
213	  have key : ∀ y : B ⊗[A] D.descended,
214	      D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.descended.subtype.lTensor B y := by
215	    intro y
216	    rw [comparison_eq_actionMap]
217	    refine D.coaction_actionMap (sub_eq_zero.mp ?_)
218	    rw [← coactionSub_lTensor_apply]
219	    exact hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero y
220	  constructor
221	  · intro y z hyz
222	    exact hinj (by rw [← key, ← key, hyz])
223	  · intro m
224	    have hm : D.coactionSub.lTensor B (D.coaction m) = 0 := by
225	      rw [coactionSub_lTensor_apply, D.coassoc m, sub_self]
226	    obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := (hexact _).mp hm
227	    refine ⟨y, ?_⟩
228	    have hcoact : D.coaction (D.comparison y) = D.coaction m := by rw [key y, hy]
229	    have := congrArg (actionMap A B M) hcoact
230	    rwa [D.counit, D.counit] at this
231	
232	/-- The comparison isomorphism `B ⊗[A] M₀ ≃ₗ[B] M` of flat descent. -/
233	noncomputable def descentEquiv [Module.Flat A B] : B ⊗[A] D.descended ≃ₗ[B] M :=
234	  LinearEquiv.ofBijective D.comparison D.comparison_bijective
235	
236	@[simp] theorem descentEquiv_tmul [Module.Flat A B] (b : B) (m : D.descended) :
237	    D.descentEquiv (b ⊗ₜ m) = b • (m : M) := rfl
238	
239	section Amitsur
240	
241	variable [Module.FaithfullyFlat A B]
242	
243	/-- **Amitsur exactness in degrees `≤ 1`**: for a faithfully flat `A → B` and any
244	`A`-module `N`, the sequence `0 → N → B ⊗[A] N ⇉ B ⊗[A] B ⊗[A] N` is exact; here the pair
245	of arrows is encoded by the single map `coactionSub` of the canonical descent datum, whose
246	kernel is the equalizer. -/
247	theorem exact_mk_coactionSub (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
248	    Function.Exact (TensorProduct.mk A B N 1) (baseChange A B N).coactionSub := by
249	  apply (Module.FaithfullyFlat.lTensor_exact_iff_exact A B _ _).mp
250	  intro z
251	  constructor
252	  · intro hz
253	    refine ⟨actionMap A B (B ⊗[A] N) z, ?_⟩
254	    have hx := (baseChange A B N).coaction_actionMap (x := z) (sub_eq_zero.mp (by
255	      rw [← coactionSub_lTensor_apply]; exact hz))
256	    rw [baseChange_coaction] at hx
257	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
258	    exact hx
259	  · rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩
260	    rw [coactionSub_lTensor_apply, sub_eq_zero]
261	    induction x with
262	    | zero => simp
263	    | tmul b n => simp
264	    | add x y hx hy => simp only [map_add, hx, hy]
265	
266	/-- The unit of descent: for a faithfully flat `A → B`, the canonical map identifies an
267	`A`-module `N` with the descended module of the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N`.
268	This is the degree `0` consequence of Amitsur exactness. -/
269	noncomputable def unitEquiv (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] :
270	    N ≃ₗ[A] (baseChange A B N).descended := by
271	  refine LinearEquiv.ofBijective
272	    ((TensorProduct.mk A B N 1).codRestrict (baseChange A B N).descended fun n => ?_)
273	    ⟨fun n n' h => ?_, fun y => ?_⟩
274	  · rw [mem_descended]
275	    simp
276	  · exact Module.FaithfullyFlat.tensorProduct_mk_injective (A := A) (B := B) N
277	      (congrArg Subtype.val h)
278	  · have h0 : (baseChange A B N).coactionSub (y : B ⊗[A] N) = 0 := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp y.2
279	    obtain ⟨n, hn⟩ := (exact_mk_coactionSub N (y : B ⊗[A] N)).mp h0
280	    exact ⟨n, Subtype.ext hn⟩
281	
282	@[simp] theorem unitEquiv_apply_coe (N : Type u) [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] (n : N) :
283	    (unitEquiv (A := A) (B := B) N n : B ⊗[A] N) = 1 ⊗ₜ n := rfl
284	
285	variable {N : Type u} [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N]
286	
287	/-- **Uniqueness of descent**: if `N` is an `A`-module and `e : B ⊗[A] N ≃ₗ[B] M`
288	intertwines the canonical descent datum on `B ⊗[A] N` with `D`, then `N` is canonically
289	`A`-isomorphic to the descended module of `D`.  In particular two descents of the same
290	datum are canonically isomorphic (compose one such equivalence with the inverse of the
291	other). -/
292	noncomputable def equivDescended (e : (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] M)
293	    (he : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] N,
294	      D.coaction (e x) = ((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B
295	        ((baseChange A B N).coaction x)) :
296	    N ≃ₗ[A] D.descended := by
297	  refine (unitEquiv N).trans <|
298	    ((e.restrictScalars A).submoduleMap (baseChange A B N).descended).trans
299	      (LinearEquiv.ofEq _ _ ?_)
300	  have hinj : Function.Injective
301	      (((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B) := by
302	    rw [LinearMap.baseChange_eq_ltensor]
303	    exact Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap _ e.injective
304	  ext m
305	  simp only [Submodule.mem_map]
306	  constructor
307	  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
308	    rw [mem_descended] at hx ⊢
309	    change D.coaction (e x) = 1 ⊗ₜ (e x)
310	    rw [he x, hx]
311	    simp
312	  · intro hm
313	    refine ⟨e.symm m, ?_, e.apply_symm_apply m⟩
314	    rw [mem_descended] at hm ⊢
315	    apply hinj
316	    have := he (e.symm m)
317	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply] at this
318	    rw [← this, hm]
319	    simp
320	
321	@[simp] theorem equivDescended_apply_coe (e : (B ⊗[A] N) ≃ₗ[B] M)
322	    (he : ∀ x : B ⊗[A] N,
323	      D.coaction (e x) = ((e : B ⊗[A] N →ₗ[B] M).restrictScalars A).baseChange B
324	        ((baseChange A B N).coaction x)) (n : N) :
325	    (D.equivDescended e he n : M) = e (1 ⊗ₜ n) := rfl
326	
327	end Amitsur
328	
329	end DescentDatum
330	
331	end Module

theorem congr_trans (f₁ : M ≃ₗ[A] P) (f₂ : P ≃ₗ[A] P') (g₁ : N ≃ₗ[R] Q) (g₂ : Q ≃ₗ[R] Q') :
    congr (f₁.trans f₂) (g₁.trans g₂) = (congr f₁ g₁).trans (congr f₂ g₂) :=
  LinearEquiv.toLinearMap_injective <| map_comp _ _ _ _

theorem congr_symm (f : M ≃ₗ[A] P) (g : N ≃ₗ[R] Q) : congr f.symm g.symm = (congr f g).symm := rfl

@[simp]
theorem congr_one : congr (1 : M ≃ₗ[A] M) (1 : N ≃ₗ[R] N) = 1 := congr_refl

theorem congr_mul (f₁ f₂ : M ≃ₗ[A] M) (g₁ g₂ : N ≃ₗ[R] N) :
    congr (f₁ * f₂) (g₁ * g₂) = congr f₁ g₁ * congr f₂ g₂ := congr_trans _ _ _ _

@[simp] theorem congr_tmul (f : M ≃ₗ[A] P) (g : N ≃ₗ[R] Q) (m : M) (n : N) :
    congr f g (m ⊗ₜ n) = f m ⊗ₜ g n :=
  rfl

@[simp] theorem congr_symm_tmul (f : M ≃ₗ[A] P) (g : N ≃ₗ[R] Q) (p : P) (q : Q) :
    (congr f g).symm (p ⊗ₜ q) = f.symm p ⊗ₜ g.symm q :=
  rfl

theorem congr_eq (f : M ≃ₗ[R] P) (g : N ≃ₗ[R] Q) :
    congr f g = TensorProduct.congr f g := rfl

variable (R A M)

/-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.rid`. -/
protected def rid : M ⊗[R] R ≃ₗ[A] M :=
  LinearEquiv.ofLinear
    (lift <| Algebra.lsmul _ _ _ |>.toLinearMap |>.flip)
    (mk R A M R |>.flip 1)
    (LinearMap.ext <| one_smul _)
    (ext fun _ _ => smul_tmul _ _ _ |>.trans <| congr_arg _ <| mul_one _)

/-- The heterobasic version of `rid` coincides with the regular version. -/
theorem rid_eq_rid : AlgebraTensorModule.rid R R M = TensorProduct.rid R M := rfl

variable {R M} in
@[simp]
theorem rid_tmul (r : R) (m : M) : AlgebraTensorModule.rid R A M (m ⊗ₜ r) = r • m := rfl

variable {M} in
@[simp]
theorem rid_symm_apply (m : M) : (AlgebraTensorModule.rid R A M).symm m = m ⊗ₜ 1 := rfl

end

section CommSemiring

section assoc
variable [Module R P] [IsScalarTower R A P]
variable [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower A B M]

/-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.assoc`:

`B`-linear equivalence between `(M ⊗[A] P) ⊗[R] Q` and `M ⊗[A] (P ⊗[R] Q)`.

Note this is especially useful with `A = R` (where it is a "more linear" version of
`TensorProduct.assoc`), or with `B = A`. -/
def assoc : (M ⊗[A] P) ⊗[R] Q ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[A] (P ⊗[R] Q) :=
  LinearEquiv.ofLinear
    (lift <| lift <| lcurry R A B P Q _ ∘ₗ mk A B M (P ⊗[R] Q))
    (lift <| uncurry R A B P Q _ ∘ₗ curry (mk R B _ Q))
    (by ext; rfl)
    (by ext; rfl)

variable {M P N Q}

@[simp]
theorem assoc_tmul (m : M) (p : P) (q : Q) :
    assoc R A B M P Q ((m ⊗ₜ p) ⊗ₜ q) = m ⊗ₜ (p ⊗ₜ q) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem assoc_symm_tmul (m : M) (p : P) (q : Q) :
    (assoc R A B M P Q).symm (m ⊗ₜ (p ⊗ₜ q)) = (m ⊗ₜ p) ⊗ₜ q :=
  rfl

/-- The heterobasic version of `assoc` coincides with the regular version. -/
theorem assoc_eq : assoc R R R M P Q = TensorProduct.assoc R M P Q := rfl

theorem rTensor_tensor [Module R P'] [IsScalarTower R A P'] (g : P →ₗ[A] P') :
    g.rTensor (M ⊗[R] N) =
      assoc R A A P' M N ∘ₗ map (g.rTensor M) id ∘ₗ (assoc R A A P M N).symm.toLinearMap :=
  TensorProduct.ext <| LinearMap.ext fun _ ↦ ext fun _ _ ↦ rfl

end assoc

section cancelBaseChange
variable [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower A B M]

/-- `B`-linear equivalence between `M ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] N)` and `M ⊗[R] N`.
In particular useful with `B = A`. -/
def cancelBaseChange : M ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] N) ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N :=
  letI g : (M ⊗[A] A) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N := congr (AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B M) (.refl R N)
  (assoc R A B M A N).symm ≪≫ₗ g

/-- Base change distributes over tensor product. -/
def distribBaseChange : A ⊗[R] (N ⊗[R] Q) ≃ₗ[A] (A ⊗[R] N) ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] Q) :=
  (cancelBaseChange _ _ _ _ _ ≪≫ₗ assoc _ _ _ _ _ _).symm

variable {M P N Q}

@[simp]
theorem cancelBaseChange_tmul (m : M) (n : N) (a : A) :
    cancelBaseChange R A B M N (m ⊗ₜ (a ⊗ₜ n)) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ n :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    (cancelBaseChange R A B M N).symm (m ⊗ₜ n) = m ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ n) :=
  rfl

theorem lTensor_comp_cancelBaseChange (f : N →ₗ[R] Q) :
    lTensor _ _ f ∘ₗ cancelBaseChange R A B M N =
      (cancelBaseChange R A B M Q).toLinearMap ∘ₗ lTensor _ _ (lTensor _ _ f) := by
  ext; simp

@[simp]
theorem distribBaseChange_tmul (n : N) (q : Q) (a : A) :
    distribBaseChange R A N Q (a ⊗ₜ (n ⊗ₜ q)) = (a ⊗ₜ n) ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ q) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem distribBaseChange_symm_tmul
    (n : N) (q : Q) (a b : A) :
    (distribBaseChange R A N Q).symm ((a ⊗ₜ n) ⊗ₜ (b ⊗ₜ q)) = (a * b) ⊗ₜ (n ⊗ₜ q) := by
  apply ((distribBaseChange R A N Q).apply_eq_iff_symm_apply.mp ?_).symm

section assoc
variable [Module R P] [IsScalarTower R A P]
variable [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower A B M]

/-- Heterobasic version of `TensorProduct.assoc`:

`B`-linear equivalence between `(M ⊗[A] P) ⊗[R] Q` and `M ⊗[A] (P ⊗[R] Q)`.

Note this is especially useful with `A = R` (where it is a "more linear" version of
`TensorProduct.assoc`), or with `B = A`. -/
def assoc : (M ⊗[A] P) ⊗[R] Q ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[A] (P ⊗[R] Q) :=
  LinearEquiv.ofLinear
    (lift <| lift <| lcurry R A B P Q _ ∘ₗ mk A B M (P ⊗[R] Q))
    (lift <| uncurry R A B P Q _ ∘ₗ curry (mk R B _ Q))
    (by ext; rfl)
    (by ext; rfl)

variable {M P N Q}

@[simp]
theorem assoc_tmul (m : M) (p : P) (q : Q) :
    assoc R A B M P Q ((m ⊗ₜ p) ⊗ₜ q) = m ⊗ₜ (p ⊗ₜ q) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem assoc_symm_tmul (m : M) (p : P) (q : Q) :
    (assoc R A B M P Q).symm (m ⊗ₜ (p ⊗ₜ q)) = (m ⊗ₜ p) ⊗ₜ q :=
  rfl

/-- The heterobasic version of `assoc` coincides with the regular version. -/
theorem assoc_eq : assoc R R R M P Q = TensorProduct.assoc R M P Q := rfl

theorem rTensor_tensor [Module R P'] [IsScalarTower R A P'] (g : P →ₗ[A] P') :
    g.rTensor (M ⊗[R] N) =
      assoc R A A P' M N ∘ₗ map (g.rTensor M) id ∘ₗ (assoc R A A P M N).symm.toLinearMap :=
  TensorProduct.ext <| LinearMap.ext fun _ ↦ ext fun _ _ ↦ rfl

end assoc

section cancelBaseChange
variable [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower A B M]

/-- `B`-linear equivalence between `M ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] N)` and `M ⊗[R] N`.
In particular useful with `B = A`. -/
def cancelBaseChange : M ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] N) ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N :=
  letI g : (M ⊗[A] A) ⊗[R] N ≃ₗ[B] M ⊗[R] N := congr (AlgebraTensorModule.rid A B M) (.refl R N)
  (assoc R A B M A N).symm ≪≫ₗ g

/-- Base change distributes over tensor product. -/
def distribBaseChange : A ⊗[R] (N ⊗[R] Q) ≃ₗ[A] (A ⊗[R] N) ⊗[A] (A ⊗[R] Q) :=
  (cancelBaseChange _ _ _ _ _ ≪≫ₗ assoc _ _ _ _ _ _).symm

variable {M P N Q}

@[simp]
theorem cancelBaseChange_tmul (m : M) (n : N) (a : A) :
    cancelBaseChange R A B M N (m ⊗ₜ (a ⊗ₜ n)) = (a • m) ⊗ₜ n :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem cancelBaseChange_symm_tmul (m : M) (n : N) :
    (cancelBaseChange R A B M N).symm (m ⊗ₜ n) = m ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ n) :=
  rfl

theorem lTensor_comp_cancelBaseChange (f : N →ₗ[R] Q) :
    lTensor _ _ f ∘ₗ cancelBaseChange R A B M N =
      (cancelBaseChange R A B M Q).toLinearMap ∘ₗ lTensor _ _ (lTensor _ _ f) := by
  ext; simp

@[simp]
theorem distribBaseChange_tmul (n : N) (q : Q) (a : A) :
    distribBaseChange R A N Q (a ⊗ₜ (n ⊗ₜ q)) = (a ⊗ₜ n) ⊗ₜ (1 ⊗ₜ q) :=
  rfl

@[simp]
theorem distribBaseChange_symm_tmul
    (n : N) (q : Q) (a b : A) :
    (distribBaseChange R A N Q).symm ((a ⊗ₜ n) ⊗ₜ (b ⊗ₜ q)) = (a * b) ⊗ₜ (n ⊗ₜ q) := by
  apply ((distribBaseChange R A N Q).apply_eq_iff_symm_apply.mp ?_).symm
